display_name: lemonade-burn CUDA (MoE on one or more NVIDIA GPUs)

support.note: Run on Tesla P100 (sm_60), RTX 2060 and Tesla T10 (sm_75). Kernels are compiled at run time by NVRTC, so newer cards may work, but none has been tested.

notes: Matches the CUDA lemonade-burn-server seats the CESARops fleet runs: Tiel-Coder and Qwen3.6 35B-A3B on cesarops4 (:8130, :8132) and LFM2.5-24B-A2B on cesarops2 (:8122).
Uses {ctx} resolved by lemond and {gpu_uuids} from AdapterServer's GPU inventory: adapter plane only (targets), no generated C++.

Packaging: lemonade-burn-server, NVRTC (libnvrtc.so.12*, libnvrtc-builtins.so.12*) and cuda-path/nvvm/libdevice/libdevice.10.bc sit in one folder (library_dir: binary puts only that folder on the loader path). The host needs only the NVIDIA driver. Without libdevice every kernel that calls exp fails to compile; lemonade-burn builds from a98831f (2026-11-17) find cuda-path/ beside the binary (or beside its bin/ folder) themselves, older builds need CUDA_PATH set to it.

GPU budget: --gpu-budget-mb 14500 and --gpu-dense-mb 900 are sized for one 16 GB card (P100, T10) and put LFM2.5-24B-A2B's experts on the GPU (88.8 tok/s decode on a P100, against 3.4 tok/s with the CPU default of 0). For a smaller card override the arguments with the model's adapter_args option or add LB_EXPERT_VRAM_MIB (MiB) to env. qwen35moe models ignore both flags and split every layer across the listed cards (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on P100 + T10: 58-73 tok/s).
LB_QW_PREFILL_CHUNK=256 keeps qwen35moe models from running out of memory on the second long prompt when the weights nearly fill the cards; LFM2 models ignore it.
Not settable from a spec (outside the plane's environment allowlist): QWEN_SPLIT (layer split across cards; the engine splits automatically without it) and CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION.
